Collateral from proposal to release

After this lesson you can:
  • Model collateral independently from a loan
  • Trace valuation, eligibility and monitoring
  • Define substitution and release controls

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. A linked lifecycle
  2. Value is dated evidence
  3. After disbursement
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. A linked lifecycle

A collateral record identifies asset, owner, location, type and links to facilities.

Proposal, verification, acceptance, charge creation, monitoring, enforcement and release are separate states.

One asset can support several exposures only under explicit ranking and coverage rules.

2. Value is dated evidence

Market value, realisable value and eligible value serve different purposes.

Valuer independence, report expiry, haircut, margin and LTV must be versioned.

Gold purity, vehicle depreciation, property title, equipment inspection and receivable ageing require product-specific evidence.

3. After disbursement

Insurance renewal, inspection, covenant, impairment and revaluation can trigger top-up, substitution, referral or recall. Release requires paid/authorised exposure, maker-checker, original-document custody and borrower acknowledgement; partial release requires remaining-coverage proof.

Regulatory anchors

  • CERSAI-CKYC — Security-interest registration and satisfaction accompany the collateral lifecycle.
  • RBI-IT-GRC — Valuation, custody and release need controlled evidence.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability COL-001 — Collateral master.
  • Capability COL-004 — Valuation lifecycle.
  • Capability COL-006 — Coverage policy.
  • Capability COL-007 — Insurance.
  • Capability COL-010 — Custody and release.
  • Capability COL-012 — Monitoring.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Can a five-year-old valuation support a new draw automatically?

  1. Yes if the asset is unchanged
  2. No; valuation currency and policy must be satisfied
  3. Only for property
  4. Only below the original limit
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Value is dated evidence and must meet current policy.
